positiveMechanism: Milestone-based public funding can support local wafer capacity and supply-chain localization.
A second Taiwan issuer demonstrates the policy-to-capacity schema is not TSMC-specific.
Government award and company facility/product evidence can be joined without inventing HVM.
negativeControls: Private capital commitment growth from US$3.94bn to US$7.94bn is not evidence that subsidy disbursement increased by the same amount.
A final award and named facility do not prove current HVM or qualified capacity.
A stale official company page can establish facility/product identity but not a reliable current production clock.
Policy support may accelerate localization while creating execution, utilization and cost risks; subsidy is not automatically margin-accretive.
Silicon-wafer supply-chain benefits cannot be generalized to all Taiwan semiconductor issuers.
pitRules: Separate preliminary terms, final award, capital commitment, disbursement, construction, qualification and HVM clocks.
